articles.title: Georgia Voll’s quickfire century lifts Australia to ODI series win against Bangladesh
articles.summary: Bangladesh 220-6; Australia 221-1 | Australia win by nine wickets. Voll’s unbeaten 131 off 97 helps hosts take unassailable 2-0 series lead. Opener Georgia Voll smashed her third ODI century in just her 15th match to secure Australia a comfortable nine-wicket win over Bangladesh and a series…
body: Earlier, Bangladesh centurion Sobhana Mostary played one of the great ODI knocks to lift the visitors to 220-6 as records tumbled at Brisbane’s Allan Border Field.

Mostary, 24, made a magnificent 118 off 134 deliveries and with her captain Nigar Sultana (74no off 114) added 195 for the fourth wicket – the highest partnership against Australia in women’s ODI history.

But making a mockery of the run chase, Voll and Phoebe Litchfield added 162 off just 119 deliveries in an opening stand that combined brute strength and creativity to the maximum, setting Australia up for an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series.

Litchfield (70 off 51) played strokes all around the ground in her entertaining knock while Voll’s power game came to the fore as she bludgeoned anything loose. Voll’s unbeaten 131 off 97 deliveries became the highest individual women’s ODI total at the venue, breaking a record Mostary had equalled only hours earlier.

articles.title: European football: Freiburg move top of Bundesliga while Isco keeps Betis flying high
articles.summary: Goto seals late 2-1 win over Schalke for 10-man Freiburg. Lazio join Inter at top of Serie A as Roma held at Como. Ten-man Freiburg scored an 85th-minute winner ⁠through Keisuke Goto to snatch a 2-1 home victory over ⁠ Schalke 04 ⁠on ​Sunday and move top of the Bundesliga.
body: Freiburg, who had ⁠already made a club-record start with 10 points from their opening ⁠four matches, climbed to 13 points, ​ahead of Borussia ‌Dortmund on ‌goal difference. The champions, Bayern Munich, who drew 2-2 ‌against Augsburg on Saturday, are third on 11.

With Freiburg in control, Maximilian Eggestein put the hosts in front after 10 minutes, but Schalke hit ‌back through Adrian Gantenbein on the half-hour. Freiburg were reduced to ​10 men when Yuito Suzuki received a second yellow card in the 64th minute, seemingly handing Schalke the initiative.

But ⁠the visitors were far too passive and ​toothless ​in attack to ​make the extra man count ​and Freiburg ‌punished them ​five ​minutes before the end with the Japan international Goto snatching the winner with a glancing header.
Borussia Mönchengladbach remained rock bottom of the Bundesliga after a 2-1 defeat to local rivals Cologne on Sunday, in a match overshadowed by ugly scenes on the terraces.

articles.title: NFL roundup: Daniels’ overtime blunder costs Commanders as Giants salvage wild 27-27 tie
articles.summary: Daniels’ late scramble leaves Washington unable to kick. Giants rally from 14 down but settle for 27-27 draw. Maye throws four TDs as Patriots rout Raiders 45-17. Jaguars stun Eagles in London with one second left.
body: Jayden Daniels took off on an ill-advised scramble in the closing seconds of overtime with the Commanders in field-goal range, and Washington were unable to stop the clock before time expired, settling for a 27-27 tie with the New York Giants on Sunday after both teams made critical mistakes in the extra period.

Washington (1-3-1) got the ball with two minutes left in overtime when Daron Payne stripped the ball from Cam Skattebo with the Giants in range for a game-winning field goal. Daniels quickly moved the Commanders to the Giants’ 24-yard line, but with 12 seconds left and Washington out of timeouts, he held on to the ball and went down for no gain. Washington lined up to spike the ball, but the clock ticked down to zero and coach Dan Quinn ripped off his headset in disgust.

The Commanders had led by two touchdowns in the fourth quarter before Jameis Winston led a furious comeback for the NFC East-leading Giants (3-1-1). He connected with Isaiah Likely for a 17-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter – Likely’s second touchdown catch of the game – and then found Malik Nabers for the tying score, also from 17 yards, with 1:43 remaining.

articles.title: Canelo Álvarez ‘fears nothing’ and will fight in Riyadh despite deadly attacks, Al-Sheikh says
articles.summary: Álvarez vows to fight in Riyadh despite deadly strikes. Airport attacks leave at least 12 dead, hundreds hurt. Mexican seeks redemption after Crawford defeat. Canelo Álvarez intends to go ahead with his world title fight in Saudi Arabia later this month despite a series of deadly attacks on…
body: The Mexican superstar is slated to challenge the unbeaten Christian Mbilli for the WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh on 31 October, three weeks after Saturday’s missile strike on the Saudi capital’s main international airport killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300.

Al-Sheikh, the chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority, said on Sunday that Álvarez had personally assured him he remained committed to the bout regardless of the fraught security situation.

“Canelo reached out and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens,” Al-Sheikh wrote on social media. “He fears nothing. My country is home to the two Holy Mosques, land of peace, safety, rich civilization, deep history and kind-hearted people. Thank you to everyone who checked in and showed support. Hard times reveal true friends.”

articles.title: 49ers' Dre Greenlaw ejected after headbutting Seahawks player in sideline skirmish
articles.summary: SEATTLE - A week after Dre Greenlaw managed to keep his sky-high emotions mostly under control, the combustible San Francisco 49ers linebacker was ejected Sunday after exploding on the Seahawks' sideline.
body: Greenlaw, 29, earned his third career ejection after he headbutted helmet-less Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones in the face after he was assessed a personal-foul penalty for hitting quarterback Sam Darnold out of bounds at the end of a 5-yard scramble in the second quarter.
After drilling Darnold, Greenlaw was surrounded by Seahawks around their bench. After exchanging words with Jones, he headbutted Jones in the face with his facemask.

Greenlaw is known for struggling to keep his emotions under wraps. He was ejected from a game in 2023 for making contact with an Eagles staffer on the sideline. He was ejected in 2022 for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. The 49ers are 48-20 when Greelaw plays.

Greenlaw has eight career unnecessary roughness penalties and four personal-foul facemask penalties in 77 games. Last week, in the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos, Greenlaw repeatedly yelled at Broncos head coach Sean Payton, telling the Chronicle he felt Payton disrespected him last year in his lone season in Denver.

articles.summary: UFC Vegas 122 went down last night inside Meta Apex in Las Vegas, Nevada, which saw Brendan Allen defeat Christian Leroy Duncan via fifth-round submission ( see it here ) in the main event of the evening.
body: Allen locked down his fourth straight win after choking out Duncan, firmly cementing his spot in the Top 5 at 185 pounds. As far as what could be next for him, perhaps a showdown against former division king, Dricus du Plessis, is in order. “DDP” is currently ranked No. 2 in the division, but his most recent win over Kamaru Usman is not enough to get him back to another title shot. He will need at least one more win to get there. On the flip side, if Allen can take out the former champion, then his championship fight dreams get one step closer. The two men have a built-in beef, so this fight sells itself.

Herbert secured his first-ever back-to-back win streak inside the Octagon after defeating Matheus Camilo, which is hard to believe since he has been fighting for the promotion for six years. Nevertheless, he is now 3-1 in his last four and he will look to build off that momentum to improve his streak to three. A fight against Zhu sounds interesting since the Chinese-born combatant is also on a nice run, having won his last four fights inside the Octagon.

articles.title: Dre Greenlaw ejected from 49ers-Seahawks game for sideline headbutt
articles.summary: Officials ejected San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw from Sunday's game against the Seahawks after they caught the linebacker headbutting an opposing player on the sideline. The incident happened about midway through the second quarter.
body: One of the first players to try and get in Greenlaw's face was Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones IV. As the Seahawks player got close to Greenlaw, the San Francisco linebacker then threw his head forward, colliding with the incoming opponent's head. At that point, Greenlaw found himself completely surrounded by navy jerseys.

For a moment it looked like Greenlaw was going to get away with it. As replays on the Fox broadcast showed the linebacker's headbutt, the only thing that officials flagged was the hit on Darnold, and nothing else. But after a minute or two, the officials made a subsequent announcement: No. 57 was disqualified. Greenlaw did not protest the flag as the broadcast showed him miming exactly what he did to Fred Warner shortly before heading off the field.

articles.title: Man City defiant and top of the table - but Anfield delivers its own verdict
articles.summary: The chant from The Kop went up early. "You haven't won a trophy since 1976." It was a reference to Manchester City's League Cup triumph, the last major honour that the club picked up prior to the period of ownership that now finds itself under such scrutiny.
body: As it is, City remain top of the table having won six games from six. But this victory will not quieten the noise. They departed to boos and the accusations of cheating that were a feature of the day.

Liverpool, three times runners-up to Manchester City in 2014, 2019 and 2022, made for perfect but hostile hosts, with the Anfield crowd perhaps the ideal outlet for the emotions, a proxy for supporters everywhere. It was an atmosphere like no other.

The enterprising flag and scarf sellers in Liverpool were certainly prepared, with an unusual emphasis on the visitors, this being City's first game since an independent commission judged that they broke Premier League rules between 2009 and 2018.

But the court of opinion is making its voice heard too. Anfield has made up its mind. The banners referred to "a generation of supporters cheated" and a playful take on Wonderwall with the amended line that "you really robbed us all".

articles.title: Nic Anderson left LSU win with injury just days before his return to Oklahoma
articles.summary: Kentucky Wildcats wide receiver Nic Anderson left Saturday night’s 35-34 overtime win over the No. 10 LSU Tigers in the second half and did not return. UK radio’s Dick Gabriel reported during the game that Anderson was being evaluated for a shoulder injury and was questionable to return, though the…
body: The timing is rough, because Anderson had just started to look like the receiver Kentucky hoped it was getting.

Through his first four games as a Wildcat, Anderson had four catches for 40 yards. Then he went to Columbia and broke out with five catches for 80 yards and his first touchdown in Kentucky blue in the 35-34 overtime win at South Carolina. That game also pushed him past 1,000 career receiving yards. It was his first touchdown since September 2025.

He stayed hot early against LSU and led all Kentucky receivers at halftime with three catches for 29 yards. The LSU game was personal, too. Anderson spent last season in Baton Rouge, playing for the same staff that included current Kentucky offensive coordinator Joe Sloan.

Before LSU, Anderson spent three years at Oklahoma, where he stuck with the program through the coaching change from Lincoln Riley to Brent Venables. His redshirt freshman season in 2023 was a breakout. He caught 38 passes for 798 yards and 10 touchdowns, averaging a team-high 21 yards per catch. Kentucky travels to Norman on Saturday (7:30 p.m. ET, SEC Network), and his homecoming is now in question.

articles.title: 'Barely a foul' - Carra criticises 'shocking' Gravenberch red card decision
articles.summary: Ryan Gravenberch's sending off in Liverpool's 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City was a "shocking decision" by referee Chris Kavanagh, according to Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.
body: Gravenberch, the standout player for an hour, was shown red after receiving a second yellow for a challenge on Jeremy Doku with the game tied at 0-0 in a flashpoint that turned the game, which had been finely poised, in City's favour.

Erling Haaland's opener came just two minutes and 37 seconds after Gravenberch was dismissed, and within six minutes Doku had doubled City's advantage before Rayan Cherki added a third with 12 minutes to play.
Gravenberch had picked up his first caution shortly after the restart for a foul on City midfielder Elliot Anderson, which Sky Sports pundit Carragher described as a "nothing challenge".

"It's such a poor decision by the referee," Carragher said after the game. "The thing that frustrates me is that he wasn't going to give a yellow card. He only gives it when he thinks Anderson is hurt.

articles.title: Greaves ends Women's Series season with record-breaking win
articles.summary: Beau Greaves ended her 2026 PDC Women's Series season with a record-breaking streak of victories on the way to two tournament wins at Event 23 and 24 in Wigan.
body: Greaves - who had already claimed back-to-back titles in Event 21 and 22 on Saturday - averaged 98.75 on the way to her third successive competition title at Event 23, marking the highest event-winning average in the history of the Women's Series.

The Yorkshire native - who has won 17 out of a possible 24 Women's Series events this year - won all of her first four matches by a 4-0 scoreline, posting a stunning 103.66 average in her victory against Steph Clark.

She lost her first legs of the day in her 5-2 victory against Gemma Hayter in the quarter-finals, before beating Fallon Sherrock - who confirmed her own return to the World Darts Championship on Saturday - in the semi-final.

Her 5-3 victory against Jade Gofford in the final confirmed her first title of the day, before beating Laura van den Berg, Sara Walton, Vicky Martin and Lauren Bloomfield to reach the quarter-finals of event 24.
